title: EIF benchmark fixture manifest
description: One manifest.json per fixture under docs/benchmarks/fixtures/<task_id>/. Declares everything eif_benchmark.py needs to materialize the fixture, run the deterministic test suite, verify the anti-cheating mutation check, and enforce budgets - without hand-reading the fixture's own source. validate-manifest checks a fixture directory against this schema plus structural checks (referenced files actually exist, digest actually matches).

task_id.description: Matches the corpus numbering in docs/benchmarks/README.md, e.g. 'T02'.

supported_modes.description: Which modes this fixture can run. C/D require the explicit integration-report, graph-artifact, runner-consumption and attempt-telemetry contracts documented in docs/benchmarks/README.md.

task_prompt_path.description: Path, relative to the fixture directory, to the exact task prompt file given to the agent.

source_dir.description: Path, relative to the fixture directory, to the immutable source tree materialize copies into the work directory.

source_digest.description: Combined sha256 over the sorted (path, sha256) manifest of every file under source_dir - computed by eif_benchmark.py, not hand-typed. validate-manifest recomputes and compares; a mismatch is a hard failure (the fixture drifted since this manifest was written).

test_command.description: Argv (not a shell string) to run the deterministic test suite against the materialized work directory, e.g. ['python', 'tests/test_fix.py']. Must be deterministic - same input tree, same result, every time.

tests_total.description: Exact expected count from a correct fix - validate-result cross-checks the emitted record's metrics.tests_total against this.

description.description: What the mutation does in plain language, e.g. 'reverts the produced fix to the original buggy line'.

mutation_command.description: Argv that, run against a WORKING (tests-passing) solution, deliberately breaks it in the one specific way this fixture is designed to catch - proving the test suite actually exercises the fix rather than passing regardless (anti-cheating).

expected_tests_passed_after_mutation.description: How many tests should still pass after the mutation is applied to an otherwise-correct solution - normally less than expected_output_contract.tests_total, proving the mutated case is genuinely caught.

license.description: License of the fixture's own source content (not EIF's license) - e.g. 'Apache-2.0' for originally-authored fixtures, or the upstream license if adapted from a public source (with provenance below naming that source).

provenance.description: Where this fixture's scenario came from - 'originally authored for this benchmark' or a named public source. Never a private repository or customer artifact - see no_private_content_confirmed.

no_private_content_confirmed.description: Must be explicitly true - a fixture manifest without this (or with it false) fails validate-manifest outright. Exists so 'no private content' is a checked fact, not an assumption (see D-12).

known_failed_fix.description: For a fixture whose task is specifically 'avoid repeating a known failed fix' (e.g. T07) - describes the documented prior wrong attempt and how to detect its recurrence. Absent for fixtures with no such history.

detection_command.description: Argv that exits non-zero if the produced solution repeats the documented known-failed approach - run by validate-result in addition to test_command.
